sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19-08-2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19-08-2022 at about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing No. KA-41-S-6678 as a pillion rider to go to Shivagange which was ridden by his friend and when they reached Kudur- Shivagange road, near Thoreramanahalli, Kudur hobli, Magadi taluk, Ramanagara district, at that time the rider of the said motorcycle ridden the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and fell on the side of the road.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries over right femur fracture and injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwari hospital wherein first aid was given and shifted to Hemavathi hospital, Tumkur wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards conveyance,
nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 21 years and doing agricultural work and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is suffered permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.
The Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statements by denying the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further contended that by colluding with the insured, the complaint was filed with delay of 15 days.
Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-41-S-6678 and its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further has denied the cause and manner of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant, imaginary and fanciful.
Hence, this respondent No.2 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

Further, Dr.Nagaraj B N is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 & 16.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Kamala who was the mother of the petitioner.

The Ex.P3 mahazar shows that from the accident spot towards its western side road edge it is 3 feet, which shows that the rider of motor cycle came in rash and negligent manner and thereby the motorcycle got skid and fell on the side of the road, thereby the petitioner being pillion rider got injuries.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 15 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

12. No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 19-08-2022, but the FIR was lodged on 04-09-2022 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 17 days of occurrence of the accident.

But the petitioner in his cross-examination has stated that soon after the accident he got admitted to the hospital and his father has got paralysis as such his mother was attending his father due to which the complaint was given after 15 days.

In this regard if we see the Ex.P1 FIR and Ex.P-2 complaint, the informant of Ex.P2 has given the details as to why the FIR was lodged belatedly by narrating that soon after the accident the petitioner Govardhana was initially admitted to Hemavathi hospital and as there was no one to take care of his son they are giving the complaint belatedly.
Thereby the said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
The endeavor of the parents will be getting the treatment to the injured son than thinking about the legal formalities.

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me) Hence the delay of 15 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.

13. It is interesting to note that no doubt the FIR was lodged belatedly, but in all the medical records, it is clearly mentioned that the history narrated to the doctors by injured at the very first Govardhana S vs Ramaiah T on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78298761/
4 instance, as can be seen from Ex.P.6 wound certificate is that injuries were sustained in an RTA.
This version has not changed since then; and even in FIR the very same version can be seen.
Under such circumstances, this court is of the firm opinion that the delay is certainly backed by genuine reasons.

Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioner after the accident.

14. In support of their defence the summons were taken by the respondent No.2 insurance company by summoning the mother of the petitioner and one Yogesh who is allegedly riding the bike at the time of accident.

The mother of the petitioner examined as RW.1 where she deposed by stating that as the petitioner admitted in the hospital and as her husband suffering from paralysis she has given the complaint after 15 days.
By treating the said witness as hostile witness the RW.1 was cross examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company.
In the cross-examination also the RW.1 answered that the petitioner got injuries on 19-08-2022 while he was going in a bike as a pillion rider and Yogesh was riding the said bike.

Further the RW.1 also answered that as the petitioner was under the treatment and also as her husband was suffering from paralysis she was unable to give complaint immediately after the accident or immediately after the discharge of the petitioner from the hospital.
15. The said witness is examined infavour of respondent No.2 insurance company.

At the time of cross-examination of the RW.1 she has answered that she has no problem to produce the documents to show that her husband is suffering from paralysis and was under the treatment for paralysis at the time of accident.
It is very important to note that the respondent No.2 insurance company filed IA by praying to issue summons to RW.1 and on the basis of said IA the summons was issued.
In the result the witness ie., mother of the petitioner examined as the witness of respondent No.2 insurance company.
The IA No.3 was filed by the respondent No.2 to summon the Kamalamma to depose evidence in this case.
On the basis of said IA the summons was issued and Kamalamma appeared and deposed in support of the complaint given by her as per Ex.P2.
The summons were not issued to the Kamalamma to produce the documents to show the health condition of her husband.
No steps were taken by the respondent No.2 insurance company to disbelieve the contention of Kamalamma in respect of her husband's health condition.

16. The rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA.41.S.6678 also examined by the respondent No.2 insurance company as RW.2, wherein RW.2 also deposed by stating that he was riding the bike on the date of accident.
The RW.2 was cross examined at length but nothing is elicited to hold that RW.2 was not riding the said bike.

17. In the cross-examination the RW.2 answered that the said bike bearing No. KA.41.S.6678 belongs to the uncle of the petitioner, but PW.1 at the time of cross- examination stated that the said bike belongs to the relative of RW.2 Yogesh.

Thereby in lieu of contradiction on the ownership of the said bike it is stated by the respondent No.2 insurance company that even though RW.2 was not riding the bike he is falsely implicated as a rider as he is having the DL.
Only on the said contradiction it cannot be stated that the vehicle is not involved in the accident.

sentences.text: 18. The investigation officer is examined as RW.3 who deposed that they have received the oral intimation on 19-08-2020 but they have not received any written intimation and they had not made any efforts to go to the hospital and collect the statement of the injured after the receipt of oral intimation.

In the cross-examination the RW.3 answered that in general after the receipt of information they will visit and record the statement of the injured and he has seized the bike in the police station premises and the said offending bike was shifted to their police station from the accident spot on 19-08-2022 itself after the accident.

By examining the evidence of RW.1 to Rw.3 the insurance company trying to establish that the RW.2 was not the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 but he is falsely implicated to get the compensation and the vehicle also falsely implicated.

19. By considering the evidence adduced by both parties the 2 short questions were involved in this case ie., firstly whether Yogesh was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 at the time of accident and secondly whether the petitioner got injuries in the accident caused by Yogesh who was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 and petitioner was proceeding in the said bike as pillion rider.
20. In this regard no doubt that the petitioner except examining himself as not examined any other eye witnesses in support of his case.
The respondent No.2 insurance company examined three witnesses in support of their defence of non involvement of motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 and also said Yogesh in the accident.

21. The RW.1 who is the mother of the petitioner appeared on the basis of summons who stated that she gave the complaint belatedly as the petitioner was hospitalised and also her husband was paralysed.
Merely because of reporting the case after 15 days the same will not make the case of the claimants as doubtful.
As stated by the RW.3 investigation officer the Ex.P4 seizure mahazar reveals that the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 was seized in the premises of the police station.

As per the evidence of RW.3 investigating officer the said motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 was shifted to their premises on the date of accident iself but he has no idea who has shifted the said bike to the police station on the date of accident itself.

22. As per Ex.P4 seizure mahazar, at the time of seizure of the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 in the presence of mahazar witnesses the IO has found the damages on the said motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678.
The Ex.P7 is the IMV report wherein it also reveals the damages on the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 .
The Ex.P4 and P7 helps the petitioner to prove the involvement of motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 in the accident.
The damages mentioned in Ex.P4 and P7 establishes that the said damages were caused on the said motorcycle in the said accident only.

sentences.text: No doubt that the MLC register extract of Hemavathi hospital is not produced by the petitioner.
But Ex.P9 Discharge summary and Ex.P6 wound certificate reveals that on 19-08-2022 itself the petitioner admitted to their hospital with history of RTA on the same day at around 7.30 p.m. near Kudur.
The respondent No.2 insurance company also not taken steps to summon the MLC register extract of Hemavathi hospital.

The IO who examined before this tribunal as RW.3 clearly answered that they have received the oral intimation and from the date of accident itself motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 was in the premises of police station.
Thereby the evidence of RW.1 to RW.3 falsifies the contention of respondent No.2 regarding the false implication of vehicle and driver.

24. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-8 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 .

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

25. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Hence the delay of 15 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and RW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint, Ex.P6 wound certificate and Ex.P9 discharge summary it cannot be considered as inordinate.

27. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19-08-2022 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-S-6678 which belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
28.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 21 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P13 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 26-01-2001, the accident was occurred on 19-08-2022, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 21 years.

In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Govardhana S vs Ramaiah T on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78298761/
8 Rajarajeshwari Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and shifted to Hemavathi hospital, Tumkur wherein he was admitted as inpatient.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 the petitioner was an inpatient from 19-08-2022 to 23-08-2022 and sustained subtrochanteric fracture right femur.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.50,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10, amounting to Rs.91,688/-.
These bills are supported by the prescriptions and advance receipts marked at Ex.P.11 & 12.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.91,700/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In this regard petitioner has not produced any documents.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2022.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 the petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi hospital for a period of 05 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 5 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500 X 4 months = Rs.62,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and through him clinical notes and X-rays were got marked at Ex.P15 & 16.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right femur subtrochanteric fracture.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of the right lower limb at 47% and whole body disability at 16%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was an agriculturist.

The alleged injuries and the evidence of the PW.2 doctor reveals that the petitioner complains of weakness and pain in right thigh, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and he cannot work like earlier.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 12% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P113, as per these documents the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 26-01-2001.
The accident was occurred in the year-2022.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 21 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.

Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 18 X 12 % =Rs.4,01,760/- which is the Govardhana S vs Ramaiah T on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78298761/
9 total loss of future income.

sentences.text: e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P9 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 05 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 05 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.5,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 05 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospitals for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
h) Future Medical Expenses:
The PW.2 doctor stated that there is a need of surgery for removal of implant which may estimate upto Rs.60,000/-.

Hence, by looking to the nature of injuries sustained and the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.

sentences.text: Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-S-6678.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-S-6678 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition by the respondent No.1.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
30.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:

3 11.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
12. No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 19-08-2022, but the FIR was lodged on 04-09-2022 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 17 days of occurrence of the accident.
But the petitioner in his cross-examination has stated that soon after the accident he got admitted to the hospital and his father has got paralysis as such his mother was attending his father due to which the complaint was given after 15 days.
Thereby the said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
The endeavor of the parents will be getting the treatment to the injured son than thinking about the legal formalities.
Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioner after the accident.
Thereby in lieu of contradiction on the ownership of the said bike it is stated by the respondent No.2 insurance company that even though RW.2 was not riding the bike he is falsely implicated as a rider as he is having the DL.
Only on the said contradiction it cannot be stated that the vehicle is not involved in the accident.
Thereby the evidence of RW.1 to RW.3 falsifies the contention of respondent No.2 regarding the false implication of vehicle and driver.
24. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-8 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA.41.S.6678 .
But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.
The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.
The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Govardhana S vs Ramaiah T on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78298761/
7 particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
26. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
27. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19-08-2022 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-S-6678 which belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 21 years.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 15 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought.
25. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
